capital.pick: Which city was the capital of {label}?
capital.match: Match each empire to its capital.
capital.reverse: Which of these empires had {value} as its capital?

rows.label: Ottoman Empire
rows.description: empire with the monarchs from the Ottoman dynasty (1299–1922)
rows.hook: was ruled by sultans and stretched across the Balkans, the Middle East and North Africa

rows.label: Roman Empire
rows.description: period of Ancient Rome following the Republic
rows.hook: was ruled by emperors like Augustus and built roads, aqueducts and the Colosseum

rows.label: Byzantine Empire
rows.description: Roman Empire during Late Antiquity and the Middle Ages
rows.hook: was the Greek-speaking eastern half of the ancient superpower and outlasted the western half by centuries

rows.label: British Empire
rows.description: overseas possessions of England and later the United Kingdom (1607–1997)
rows.hook: was the largest realm in history, famous for the saying that the sun never set on it

rows.label: German Empire
rows.description: German nation-state in Central Europe from 1871 to 1918
rows.hook: was united under the Prussian king and ruled by Kaiser Wilhelm II during the Great War

rows.label: Mongol Empire
rows.description: 13th- and 14th-century empire originating in Mongolia
rows.hook: was founded by Genghis Khan and grew into the largest contiguous land realm ever

rows.label: Russian Empire
rows.description: former empire in Eurasia and North America (1721–1917)
rows.hook: was ruled by tsars, such as Peter the Great and Catherine the Great

rows.label: Empire of Japan
rows.description: empire in the Asia-Pacific region from 1868 to 1947
rows.hook: was an island power ruled by an emperor that fought in the Pacific during the Second World War

rows.label: Umayyad Caliphate
rows.description: second Islamic caliphate (661–750 CE)
rows.hook: was the first hereditary Islamic dynasty, spreading Arabic rule from Spain to Central Asia

rows.label: Abbasid Caliphate
rows.description: third Islamic caliphate (750–1258)
rows.hook: was the Islamic dynasty of the Golden Age of scholarship, linked to the tales of Harun al-Rashid

rows.label: Inca Empire
rows.description: 1438–1533 empire in South America
rows.hook: was the Andean realm of Machu Picchu, known for its mountain roads and knotted-string record keeping

rows.label: Sasanian Empire
rows.description: last pre-Islamic Iranian empire (224–651 AD)

rows.label: First French Empire
rows.description: empire of Napoleon I of France, from 1804 to 1815
rows.hook: was the realm of a general who crowned himself emperor and was finally beaten at Waterloo

rows.label: Maurya empire
rows.description: ancient Indian empire (322–184 BCE)

rows.label: Carolingian Empire
rows.description: 800–843 final stage in the history of the early medieval realm of the Franks, ruled by the Carolingian dynasty

rows.label: Aztec Empire
rows.description: former Mesoamerican empire
rows.hook: was a Mesoamerican power conquered by Hernan Cortes and the Spanish

rows.label: Portuguese Empire
rows.description: global empire centered in Portugal (1415–1999)
rows.hook: was the first global European sea power, whose explorer Vasco da Gama first sailed from Europe to India

rows.label: Gupta Empire
rows.description: ancient Indian empire (c. 3rd century CE–575 CE)

rows.label: Second French Empire
rows.description: government of France under Napoleon III, from 1852 to 1870
rows.hook: was led by a nephew of the famous general and saw the grand rebuilding of its capital's boulevards

rows.label: Empire of Brazil
rows.description: empire in South America between 1822 and 1889
rows.hook: was the only monarchy in South America, ruled by Pedro I and Pedro II

rows.label: Songhai Empire
rows.description: former state located in western Africa
